points: The Street has already been trimming numbers, with 3 upward vs 8 downward revisions in the last 30 days and the 90-day revenue estimate down 2.14%; the Oct 22 print will show whether those cuts were deep enough or if estimates still have further to fall.
Q2 TTM EPS was $0.85, up 18.1% from $0.72 a year earlier, but the name trades at 34x forward earnings versus a sector median of 12x; Q3 needs to justify that premium or the multiple is at risk.

Reports suggest Q2 headline revenue grew 21% to $113.4m while core revenue grew only 10% and total written premium rose 14% to $1.34B; Q3 will reveal whether the gap between headline growth and underlying premium/core growth is widening.
Consensus already prices a reacceleration, with FY1 EPS up 15.5% and FY2 EPS up 25.8% to $2.70; the print and guidance will show whether that second-year jump is still intact or starting to unwind.
At 7.2x sales and a P/E of 1.6x the theme median, the market is pricing strong operating leverage; if Q3 margins or EPS do not expand, the premium multiple has little support.

GSHD reports before peers RYAN on Oct 30 and AJG on Nov 5, so its Q3 tone and guidance will set the read-through for the insurance-broker group; a soft print would reinforce the warm/lean-short theme as peers follow.
watch: Q3 total revenue growth vs core revenue growth — if core continues to lag the headline or both decelerate, the short is supported.
Total written premium growth and dollar level — a slowdown from the reported Q2 14%/$1.34B pace undermines the FY2 earnings story.
FY1/FY2 EPS guidance and revision trajectory — any cut to FY2's +25.8% growth or failure to defend FY1 $2.15 supports the short.
Forward P/E premium vs theme median — if management does not justify the 34x/1.6x premium, multiple compression drives the trade.
